evidence: the-latency-check-times-a-write: check_dd_latency.sh times a 1M dd oflag=dsync write (SIZE=1M for FILE_SIZE 1), sets WARNING when RESULT>=WARN_SEC and CRITICAL when RESULT>=CRIT_SEC, prints "$STATE - ...", rm -f the zero.img.$$ file and exits $status; so 1 5 10 gives OK rc 0, 0 0 gives CRITICAL rc 2 (>=0 always true), and no zero.img.* stays in /tmp, exactly as expected

the-reboot-check-says-ok: check_reboot_required.sh prints 'OK - No reboot required' and exits 0 unless /var/run/reboot-required exists, which it does not on the freshly applied node; probe and expect match the script verbatim

the-file-handle-check-reports-the-kernel-counts: check_file_handles.sh copies /proc/sys/fs/file-nr, echoes 'OK - ' plus the three fields (unquoted echo collapses the tabs to spaces) and '| f_handle_used=<field 1>;;;;<field 3>', exit 0; the probe's regex requires exactly that with field 3 read from the kernel, so it tests what the script declares

purpose gap: Tested on the node: installation (root 0755, module bytes, mypython shebang), the Puppet check's OK, UNKNOWN under the run lock and CRITICAL on agent exit 1 (disabled agent), reboot OK/WARNING, file-handle counts, netstat listen/established/remote-IP counts, package count OK/WARNING and the stale-list alarm, bandwidth OK/WARNING/CRITICAL (peer traffic), dd latency OK/CRITICAL, CPU OK/CRITICAL, memory OK/CRITICAL, OS release, certificate expiry wording OK/WARNING, Elasticsearch Unknown/OK/Critical; RHEL branches honestly uncovered (rhel9); the header's 'zimbra' claim has no code, rightly left out. GAP: nagios-puppet.sh has a second CRITICAL branch, 'if [ $RC -gt 2 ]' (puppet agent --test exit 4 or 6, i.e. resources that failed during the run, the main failure a Puppet monitor exists to catch); the outcome row narrows 'fails otherwise' to the disabled agent (exit 1 branch) and no check reaches the -gt 2 branch, nor is it listed uncovered, although the lab can exercise it with a node-local mutating check (e.g. drift a managed file's mode and chattr +i it so the agent's fix fails, then undo). Secondary: the Elasticsearch stand-in answers every POST without recording it, so the outcome's 'asks localhost:9200 for matching sshd events' (URL /_search?size=10, the query_string and received_at range in the body) is not probed; the stand-in could record the request.
